findings.function: fallback (SELECT callback), execute, executeWithPermit (Select.select inlined in the action loop)
findings.decompiled: call this.address with: gas (1 == n) * (gasCap ^ gas_remaining) ^ gasCap ... / t = 0 / while not ext_call.success: / if gasCap / 63 + gasCap + 8192 > gas_remaining or t + 1 == n: revert with memory ...
findings.source: Select.sol:153-169 if (_setOperatorAndTryCall(address(this), callData, ..., (!isLast).ternary(gasCap, beforeGas = gasleft()))) break; if (isLast.or(beforeGas < beforeGasThreshold)) { revert(returndata) }
findings.issue: The bytecode reads GAS once, before the trial call (pc 0x453b), and compares that same value with the threshold after the call fails (pc 0x459c dup14 gt). The text prints `gas_remaining` in the post-call test as if gas were read again after the call, so the condition that chooses between 'revert' and 'try the next candidate' reads a different (smaller) value than the bytecode uses.
findings.rule: GAS is not a pure value: when its result is used after another gas-consuming instruction (a CALL above all), bind it to a variable at the GAS instruction (beforeGas = gas_remaining) and print that variable at every later use.
findings.verified: pancxx disasm: pc 0x453b gas ... 0x4589 call ... 0x459c dup14 gt or jumpi (no second GAS)

findings.source: Select.sol:136-171 uint256 i; while (true) { ...offset[i]...; i++; bool isLast = i == n; if (tryCall) break; if (isLast || ...) revert }  |  UniswapV4.sol while (data.length >= _HOP_DATA_LENGTH) { ... }
findings.issue: The SELECT trial loop is rotated in all 9 copies: the first trial (selection, call, transient bookkeeping) is printed before the loop and repeated in the body, and the counter t is one behind the source's i (tests t + 1 == n, t + 2 == n). One of the three copies of the UniswapV4 hop loop is also rotated (its head is peeled into an 'if len >= 53' guard and the next iteration's head is printed before 'continue'), while the other two copies print 'while t >= 53'.
findings.rule: Recognise the do-while shape 'body; i = i + 1; if c(i): goto body' as one loop with its test at the place of the exit, instead of peeling an iteration; when the peeled copy and the loop body are the same statements up to the counter, fold them into one loop with the counter starting at its initial value.

findings.function: fallback, execute, executeWithPermit (UniswapV3 pool swap call, Basic/RFQ calls)
findings.source: UniswapV3Fork._uniV3ForkSwap: (bool success, bytes memory returndata) = pool.call(...) - the returndata copy is a shared compiler helper reached from several call sites
findings.issue: A phi of jump-destination constants (the return address of a shared helper) leaks into the text as a variable that is only tested to choose between three identical arms; it is also assigned under two names (_5995 is set, _5994 is tested, with no copy between them).
findings.rule: A branch whose arms are identical is its arm; a variable whose only values are code addresses and whose only uses are such branches is dead and must not be printed (more generally, never print the value of a jump destination as data).

findings.function: fallback (Take.take / Take._callSelector, about 60 calls), execute, executeWithPermit
findings.source: FlashAccountingCommon.sol:758-766 mstore(0x60, amount); mstore(0x40, to); mstore(0x2c, mul(iszero(eq(0xeee..., token)), token)); mstore(0x0c, shl(0x60, selector)); call(gas(), caller(), 0, 0x1c, 0x64, 0, 0)
findings.issue: Once the selector is recognised, the 96 argument bytes are still split along the stores (12 zero bytes, a token<<96 word, 20 bytes of 'to') instead of the three ABI words (token or 0, to, amount); the shift by 96 is printed as a multiplication by 0x1000000000000000000000000 (212 lines), and the amount as mem[96] instead of the value just stored there.
findings.rule: When a call's selector is known, re-slice its argument bytes at 32-byte boundaries after the selector and simplify each word (Bytes(12,0) ++ Bytes(20, x << 96 >> 96) is address(x)); print x * 2**k as x << k; fold a memory read through the store just before it.

notes: Reviewed by structure: the three big functions are 7,900-8,000 lines each (fallback 34-8030, executeWithPermit 8031-15916, execute 15917-23956); balanceOf checked in full (exact: Bytes(1, 0)). Checked in detail: the takerSubmitted modifier (setPayer: ConfusedDeputy, ReentrantPayer revert data - exact, the compiler keeps the source's store order so the 12 padding bytes are zero; clearPayer: PayerSpent), the empty-actions path (_checkSlippageAndTransfer with balanceOf/transfer/ETH send), executeWithPermit's permit dispatch (ERC2612 and DAI permit, PermitExpired, nonces/allowance/DOMAIN_SEPARATOR, the EIP-712 hash, ecrecover and InvalidSignature, UnsupportedPermitType/Panic(33)); the allowance revert reading 'from uint96(ptr) | ALLOWANCE_HOLDER << 96' is exact (the source's mstore(0x34, spender) clobbers the free memory pointer before mload(0x40)); the BalancerV3 callback header, Take.take (sendTo calls, ZeroBuyAmount, TooMuchSlippage), safeTransfer/TransferFailed, the callback dispatch through the transient operator slot. No semantic error found other than the GAS one. Loops: 9 explicit source loops (BalancerV3, PancakeInfinity and UniswapV4 hop loops, Take.take, Select._runActions, Select.select, Settler._execute, UniswapV3Fork._uniV3ForkSwap, Velodrome._get_y's for); Velodrome's two inner whiles are inside a /* */ comment and not counted. The 59 text whiles are all copies of these: fallback 33 (24 Take.take copies, 3 UniV4 hop copies, 1 each of the others), execute 13 and executeWithPermit 13 (_execute loop x4-5, UniV3 swap loops, Velodrome, SELECT). No spurious while. Other things not filed: 'signerN = ecrecover(...)' is unused and the check reads 'mem[ecrecover.result]' (the source's mload(staticcall(...)) idiom, exact but obscure); the base-36 Cuid.decode of the zid word (ATTEST) is an unreadable chain of '/ 2176782336 %'; 10**54 is printed in hex (P17, 40 lines); P2 also covers 46 calls whose selector is a memory slice ('call caller.mem[_5389 + 28 len 4]'). Event and error names are mostly raw selectors (not in the signature database). Immutables: none visible (no '????').
summary: A faithful but enormous transcript of assembly-heavy code: everything checked matches the bytecode except a GAS value propagated past a call in the SELECT trial loop; 50 aborted paths lose the tail of execute/executeWithPermit for most first-action types, the SELECT loop is rotated, leaked jump-address phis select between identical arms, and the mulDiv/512-bit arithmetic is unreadable.
